senses.definition: (manner) In an equal manner; in equal shares or proportion; with equal and impartial justice; evenly
examples: The pie was divided equally among the guests.
They shared equally in the spoils.

quotes.text:
And when their ſcattered armie is ſubdu’d:
And you march on their ſlaughtered carkaſſes,
Share equally the gold that bought their liues,
And liue like Gentlmen in Perſea, […]
quotes.reference: c. 1587–1588 (date written), [Christopher Marlowe], Tamburlaine the Great. […] The First Part […], 2nd edition, part 1, London: […] [R. quotes.text: You have to give them credit, rarely does a character appeal equally to four-year-old children and middle-aged aunts posting tepid jokes and fake Oscar Wilde quotes on their timelines.

senses.definition: (degree) In equal degree or extent; just as.
examples: The gas stations are equally far from the highway.

quotes.text: The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track.[…]Their example was followed by others at a time when the master of Mohair was superintending in person the docking of some two-year-olds, and equally invisible.

senses.definition: (conjunctive) Used to link two or more coordinate elements
examples: John suffered setbacks at his job. Equally, Frank's business slowed.
